{{Portal|Free software}}
The '''tidyverse''' is a collection of [[Open-source software|open source]] [[R packages|packages]] for the [[R (programming language)|R programming language]] introduced by [[Hadley Wickham]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.revolutionanalytics.com/2016/09/tidyverse.html|title=Welcome to the Tidyverse|website=Revolutions|access-date=2018-11-26}}</ref> and his team that "share an underlying design philosophy, grammar, and data structures" of [[tidy data]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tidyverse.org/|title=Tidyverse|website=www.tidyverse.org|language=en-us|access-date=2018-11-26}}</ref> Characteristic features of tidyverse packages include extensive use of non-standard evaluation and encouraging [[Pipeline (software)|piping]].<ref>{{Citation|author1=Stefan Milton Bache |author2=Hadley Wickham|title=magrittr: A Forward-Pipe Operator for R|date=2014-11-22|url=https://cran.r-project.org/package=magrittr|access-date=2020-04-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Wickham|first=Hadley|url=https://style.tidyverse.org/pipes.html|title=4 Pipes {{!}} The tidyverse style guide}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Wickham |first1=Hadley |title=Advanced R |date=May 30, 2019 |publisher=[[Chapman & Hall]] |isbn=978-0815384571 |edition=2nd |location=New York}}</ref>

As of November 2018, the tidyverse package and some of its individual packages comprise 5 out of the top 10 most downloaded R packages.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rdocumentation.org/trends|title=RDocumentation|website=www.rdocumentation.org|access-date=2018-11-26}}</ref> The tidyverse is the subject of multiple books and papers.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Duggan|first=Jim|date=2018-09-07|title=Input and output data analysis for system dynamics modelling using the tidyverse libraries of R|journal=System Dynamics Its syntax has been referred to as "supremely readable",<ref>{{Cite web |last=Steinmetz |first=Art |date=2024-04-10 |title=Outsider Data Science - The Truth About Tidy Wrappers |url=https://outsiderdata.netlify.app/posts/2024-04-10-the-truth-about-tidy-wrappers/benchmark_wrappers.html |access-date=2024-04-11 |website=outsiderdata.netlify.app |language=en}}</ref> and some<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Heppler |first=Jason |date=2018-02-27 |title=Teaching the tidyverse to R novices |url=https://medium.com/@jaheppler/teaching-the-tidyverse-to-r-novices-7747e8ce14e |access-date=2023-08-24 |website=Medium |language=en}}</ref> have argued that tidyverse is an effective way to introduce complete beginners to programming, as pedagogically it allows students to quickly begin doing  data processing tasks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=on |first=Teach the tidyverse to beginners was published |title=Teach the tidyverse to beginners |url=http://varianceexplained.org/r/teach-tidyverse/ |access-date=2022-07-15 |website=Variance Explained |date=5 July 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> Moreover, some practitioners have pointed out that data processing tasks are intuitively  easier to [[Method chaining|chain]] together with tidyverse compared to Python's equivalent data processing package, [[Pandas (software)|pandas]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why pandas feels clunky when coming from R |url=https://sumsar.net/blog/pandas-feels-clunky-when-coming-from-r/ |access-date=2024-03-30 |website=Rasmus Bååth's Blog |language=en-us}}</ref> Critics of the tidyverse have argued it promotes tools that are harder to teach and learn than their built-in, base R equivalents and are too dissimilar to some programming languages.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Matloff |first1=Norm |date=30 September 2019 |title=An opinionated view of the Tidyverse "dialect" of the R language |url=https://github.com/matloff/TidyverseSkeptic |accessdate=28 October 2019 |website=GitHub}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Muenchen |first1=Bob |date=23 March 2017 |title=The Tidyverse Curse |url=http://r4stats.com/2017/03/23/the-tidyverse-curse/ |website=r4stats.com |language=en}}</ref>

There is an active R community around the tidyverse. For example, there is the [[TidyTuesday]] social data project organised by the Data Science Learning Community (DSLC),<ref>{{Cite web |title=dslc.io |url=https://dslc.io/ |access-date=2024-08-11 |website=dslc.io |language=en}}</ref> where varied real-world datasets are released each week for the community to participate, share, practice, and make learning to work with data easier.<ref>{{Citation |title=rfordatascience/tidytuesday |date=2024-08-11 |url=https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday |access-date=2024-08-11 |publisher=Data Science Learning Community}}</ref> 

The tidyverse principles more generally encourage and help ensure that a universe of streamlined packages, in principle, will help alleviate dependency issues and compatibility with current and future features.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Power of Transitioning to a '-verse' Approach in R Package Development |url=https://www.appsilon.com/post/the-power-of-transitioning-to-a-verse |access-date=2024-08-11 |website=www.appsilon.com |language=en}}</ref>  An example of such a tidyverse principled approach is the pharmaverse, which is a collection of R packages for clinical reporting usage in the [[pharmaceutical industry]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=pharmaverse |url=https://pharmaverse.org/ |access-date=2024-08-11 |website=pharmaverse.org}}</ref>

==Packages==
The core tidyverse packages, which provide functionality to model, transform, and visualize data, include:<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tidyverse.org/packages/|title=Tidyverse packages - Tidyverse|access-date=2018-11-26|language=en-us}}</ref>
* tidyr – help transform data specifically into [[tidy data]], a table where each row is a single observation. The value of each observation is given in a column of the table. Variables describing the observation are included as additional columns.
* [[ggplot2]] – for data visualization
* [[dplyr]] – for wrangling and transforming data
* readr – help read in common delimited, text files with data
* purrr - a [[functional programming]] toolkit
* tibble – a modern implementation of the built-in data frame data structure
* stringr – helps to manipulate string data types
* forcats helps to manipulate category data types

Additional packages assist the core collection.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tidyverse packages|url=https://www.tidyverse.org/packages/|access-date=2020-12-22|website=www.tidyverse.org|language=en-us}}</ref> Other packages based on the tidy data principles are regularly developed, such as tidytext<ref>{{Citation |last=Silge |first=Julia |title=tidytext: Text mining using tidy tools |date=2023-02-01 |url=https://github.com/juliasilge/tidytext |access-date=2023-02-03}}</ref> for text analysis, tidymodels<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tidymodels |url=https://www.tidymodels.org/ |access-date=2023-02-03 |website=www.tidymodels.org |language=en-us}}</ref> for machine learning, or tidyquant<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tidy Quantitative Financial Analysis |url=https://business-science.github.io/tidyquant/ |access-date=2023-02-03 |website=business-science.github.io |language=en}}</ref> for financial operations.
